title: pairtest.py: is a predator or consumer its own individual or half of a pair? Split coincidence with host splits, contact share and lifetime host count separate c43's consumers (34/36 splits with the host), c52's predators (3/36, but one host for life) and c46's predators (0/11, free 95% of the time)
summary: Importable module and CLI for the open question in STATE.md about the ecology claims (is the guest body or the guest-host pair the individual?). From a labkit pack with two species channels it tracks both with labkit's own functions and reports: persistent guest splits within 1 frame and 20 px of a host split; the share of guest bodies touching a host; and, for guest tracks living >= L frames, how many unrelated host lineages each touches and the share of its life spent alone. On my fresh-seed packs: c52 digestion ecology (seed 9, K 20): 3/36 coincident, 88% touching, 4/306 tracks touch 2+ unrelated prey, alone 2.5% of their life; c43 CIPS consumer (seed 41, K 5): 34/36 coincident, 91% touching, 10 tracks >= 20 frames, alone 4%; c46 hunting ecology (seed 61, 256^2, K 5): 0/11 coincident, 7% touching, 106 tracks, 7 with 2+ unrelated prey, alone 95%.

tool.usage: python pairtest.py PACK_DIR WORLD.py OUT.json --host 0 --guest 1 --K 20 --dtf 100 --L 20, or import pairtest; pairtest.run(pack_dir, world_py, host=0, guest=1, K=20). Needs frames.npz with the render array (labkit keeps it locally; it is not imported to the ledger).

limits: Coincidence uses labkit frame spacing (100 t in all three worlds), so a guest split that follows a host split by more than one frame counts as not coincident (c52's predators often tear between sister prey several frames after the prey split). Host splits are any track born by a split, persistent or not. One seed per world; the three worlds use different lineage windows (K 20 vs 5). The contact test uses render > 0.5 on both channels and a 2 px dilation.
